subject: maths
question: A and B together can do a certain work in 36 days, whereas B and C together can do it 40 days. A, B and C together can do it in 30 days. B alone can do (7)/(8) part of the original work in:
solution:
Formula:

Efficiency = Total work / Time taken to complete work individually

**Concept Used:**

Assume total work days as the LCM value of the individual time required for the persons involved. 

Calculation:

Total work = LCM of 36, 40, 30 = 360 unit

Efficiency of A and B

⇒ 360over 36 = 10 units of work/day

Efficiency of B and C

⇒ 360over 40 = 9 unit of work/day

Efficiency of A, B and C

⇒ 360over 30 = 12 units of work/day

Efficiency of C = 12 - 10 = 2 units of work/day

Efficiency of B = 9 - 2 = 7 units of work/day

So, Time taken by B to complete the work = 360over 7 day

∴ Time taken to complete (7)/(8) part of the original work 

⇒ (7)/(8) × 360over 7 = 45 days.

∴ B would complete (7)/(8)th of the work in 45 days.
